name: International Securities
founded: 2001 (as First Gulf Financial Services, the brokerage arm of First Gulf Bank, now First Abu Dhabi Bank); acquired by International Holding Company (IHC) in 2019 (company says it became an IHC Group company on 1 Nov 2019)
ownership_summary: Not listed. Wholly owned by International Financial Assets Holding RSC Ltd, which is 95% owned by International Holding Company PJSC (ADX: IHC); IHC transferred its entire 100% holding to that sub-holding during 2025, so IHC's effective interest fell from 100% to 95% (IHC FY2025 financial statements).

shareholders.holder: International Financial Assets Holding RSC Ltd (95% owned by International Holding Company PJSC, ADX: IHC)

government_link: Indirect: ultimate parent International Holding Company PJSC is an ADX-listed Abu Dhabi conglomerate. IHC's own shareholder base was not assessed in this profile.
group_structure: International Securities L.L.C. (UAE share brokerage) sits under International Financial Assets Holding RSC Ltd, IHC's 95%-owned financial-services sub-holding, which also owns, for example, Funder.AI Technologies (75%) and, from 1 May 2025, 60% of Reem Finance PJSC. IHC also owns Beltone Holding (Egypt brokerage and asset management). No separate financial statements of International Securities are published; IHC consolidates it.
footprint: UAE (Abu Dhabi head office). Trades ADX, DFM and Nasdaq Dubai; its 'Tabadul Hub' gives access to Bahrain Bourse (BHB), Muscat Stock Exchange (MSX) and Astana International Exchange (AIX) from one platform. Checked 2026-10-12.
customer_segments: Retail and corporate investors in UAE equities and derivatives (individual and corporate online account opening); institutional brokerage and research clients.
business_lines: Equity brokerage on ADX, DFM and Nasdaq Dubai; single-stock futures; margin trading; short selling; securities lending and borrowing; ETFs; sukuk and bonds; cross-listed GCC access via Tabadul Hub; online trading (eTrade) and Mobile Trading app; equity research (company coverage, research library). Company claims to be the number one broker in Abu Dhabi and the UAE (ADX plus DFM) and lists awards such as 'Top Broker by Trading Value (ADX)' 2024 and 'Best Equity Broker for Abu Dhabi' 2025.

capabilities.wealth_summary: International Securities is IHC's Abu Dhabi stockbroker (founded 2001 as First Gulf Bank's brokerage arm; IHC since 2019; since 2025 held via the 95%-owned International Financial Assets Holding). It is an execution and research house for UAE equities and derivatives, with margin trading, short selling, securities lending, ETFs, sukuk/bonds and a Tabadul Hub for Bahrain, Muscat and Astana listings. Clients use the eTrade web platform and a Mobile Trading app. The website claims 42,000+ clients and 57.1bn in H1 2026 trading value (currency not stated), and it held AED 1.0bn of client cash at end-2025. No asset management, discretionary portfolios, funds shelf, structured products or international (US/EU) market access were found.

private_banking.detail: Brokerage only; no private-banking or HNW wealth proposition found.

asset_management.detail: No asset-management or portfolio-management service on the website.

digital_investing.detail: eTrade online platform and 'Mobile Trading' app (App Store/Google Play, 'intl-securities'); online KYC for individual and corporate accounts. Platform vendor not named.

islamic_wealth.detail: Sukuk are listed among tradable instruments; no Shariah-compliant product range described.

Launched 'Tabadul Hub' single-platform access to ADX, BHB, MSX and AIX (date not stated)

opportunities: Large UAE retail brokerage base (42,000+ clients claimed) with app and web platforms but no managed portfolios, funds, structured products, private markets or US/international equities found (S1, S2).
Vision statement mentions shaping 'a smarter future with Artificial Intelligence', but no AI tool is described on the site (S2).
Part of IHC's financial-services sub-holding (with Reem Finance and Funder.AI), which is building a financial-services franchise in Abu Dhabi (S4, S5).
barriers: Execution-focused, local-market strategy ('focused on the local market') per the CEO message (S4).
Decisions likely sit with IHC's financial-services sub-holding; no published board or technology leadership (S3, S5).
